stem: Lagophthalmos is:
options: inability to close the palpebral fissure.
incomplete opening of the palpebral fissure.
explanation_verbatim: Lagophthalmos is the failure of the eyelids to close completely, often due to facial nerve palsy or scarring. It can lead to exposure keratitis due to corneal drying.

Symblepharon may be caused by:
explanation_verbatim: Symblepharon is adhesion between the bulbar and palpebral conjunctiva, commonly caused by chemical burns or severe conjunctival inflammation. The scarring process leads to fusion of the conjunctival surfaces.

Astigmatism is NOT corrected by:
explanation_verbatim: Astigmatism is corrected with glasses, contact lenses, or LASIK, but not with radial keratotomy, which is designed mainly for myopia. It involves radial corneal incisions that don’t correct irregular curvature.

stem: Ptosis cannot be caused by:

explanation_verbatim: Ptosis is drooping of the upper eyelid caused by conditions like third nerve palsy, Horner’s syndrome, or trauma. A chalazion of the lower lid doesn’t affect the upper lid’s position.

Fluorescein angiography is used for studying:
explanation_verbatim: Fluorescein angiography highlights retinal and choroidal circulation, allowing assessment of vascular diseases like diabetic retinopathy or vein occlusion. It does not visualize orbital or conjunctival vessels.

explanation_verbatim: The inferior oblique muscle elevates the eye when it is adducted. It also contributes to extorsion and abduction.

stem: Phacolytic glaucoma may occur in:
Phacolytic glaucoma may occur in:
explanation_verbatim: Phacolytic glaucoma occurs when lens proteins leak through the capsule of a hypermature cataract, causing secondary open-angle glaucoma. It results in inflammation and raised IOP.

stem: Ectropion can be due to:
Ectropion can be due to:
explanation_verbatim: Ectropion is outward turning of the eyelid margin, often caused by facial nerve palsy (7th nerve). It leads to exposure and tearing due to poor lid closure.

stem: Topical corticosteroids are contraindicated in the following type of corneal ulcers:
Topical corticosteroids are contraindicated in the following type of corneal ulcers:
explanation_verbatim: Corticosteroids worsen herpes simplex keratitis (dendritic ulcer) by promoting viral replication and corneal perforation. Antiviral therapy should be used instead.

stem: Post-traumatic diplopia may be due to:
Post-traumatic diplopia may be due to:
explanation_verbatim: Iridodialysis is separation of the iris root from the ciliary body following trauma, which can cause monocular diplopia. It results in an additional pupil-like opening.

stem: A right optic tract lesion results in:
A right optic tract lesion results in:
explanation_verbatim: A right optic tract lesion affects fibers from the left visual fields of both eyes, producing left homonymous hemianopia. This occurs after the optic chiasm.

The most conclusive test for diagnosing esotropia is:
explanation_verbatim: The cover test objectively detects latent or manifest squints (like esotropia) by observing eye movement when the fellow eye is covered. It is more reliable than the corneal reflex test.

explanation_verbatim: The peaked pupil and dark body at the limbus suggest a penetrating injury with intraocular foreign body. The eye should not be manipulated—apply a shield and refer urgently.

A recurrent bilateral conjunctivitis occurring with the onset of hot weather in young boys with symptoms of burning, itching, and lacrimation with large flat topped cobble stone papillae raised areas in the palpebral conjunctiva is diagnosed as:
explanation_verbatim: Seasonal, recurrent allergic conjunctivitis in boys with cobblestone papillae on the upper tarsal conjunctiva is typical of vernal keratoconjunctivitis. It is an allergic inflammatory condition.

stem: Seeing colored halos of gradual onset and slowly progressive course in a young male with frequent changing glasses prescription is most probably:
Seeing colored halos of gradual onset and slowly progressive course in a young male with frequent changing glasses prescription is most probably:
explanation_verbatim: Gradual onset of colored halos with frequent changes in glasses in a young person suggests irregular astigmatism due to keratoconus. It’s a progressive corneal ectatic disorder.

stem: A painful , tender , non-itchy localized redness of conjunctiva can be caused by which of the folloeing pathology ?
A painful , tender , non-itchy localized redness of conjunctiva can be caused by which of the folloeing pathology ?
explanation_verbatim: Localized, tender, non-itchy redness without discharge points to episcleritis, a benign inflammation of the episcleral tissue. It’s self-limiting and less painful than scleritis.

stem: 6 years old child presented with white pupil of his right eye that appeared for the first time since 2 months following trauma to the right eye with stick. The parents assure that the vision in the affected eye was completely normal in previous examinations prior to the trauma. Which of the following pathologies is the possible cause of leukocoria in this patient?

6 years old child presented with white pupil of his right eye that appeared for the first time since 2 months following trauma to the right eye with stick. The parents assure that the vision in the affected eye was completely normal in previous examinations prior to the trauma. Which of the following pathologies is the possible cause of leukocoria in this patient?
explanation_verbatim: Sudden leukocoria (white pupil) appearing after trauma with prior normal vision is likely traumatic cataract. Retinoblastoma is excluded since vision was normal before trauma.

stem: A baby about 39 days old presents with excessive lacrimation and photophobia. He has large and hazy cornea in both eyes. His lacrimal system is normal. What is the probable diagnosis?
A baby about 39 days old presents with excessive lacrimation and photophobia. He has large and hazy cornea in both eyes. His lacrimal system is normal. What is the probable diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Photophobia, tearing, and a large hazy cornea in infancy are classic signs of congenital glaucoma due to increased IOP stretching the cornea. Early diagnosis prevents optic nerve damage.

stem: A middle aged female with recurrent joint pain gave past history of recurrent attacks of pain, redness and dropped vision in one eye. Recently she complained of similar attack. The most important diagnostic sign of activity is:

A middle aged female with recurrent joint pain gave past history of recurrent attacks of pain, redness and dropped vision in one eye. Recently she complained of similar attack. The most important diagnostic sign of activity is:
explanation_verbatim: Active uveitis (iridocyclitis) shows inflammatory cells and protein in the anterior chamber (“flare”). These indicate current activity requiring anti-inflammatory treatment.

stem: A one-month old baby is brought with complaints of photophobia and watering. Clinical examination shows normal tear passages and clear but large cornea. The most likely diagnosis is:
A one-month old baby is brought with complaints of photophobia and watering. Clinical examination shows normal tear passages and clear but large cornea. The most likely diagnosis is:
explanation_verbatim: An enlarged, clear cornea in a one-month-old with photophobia suggests buphthalmos, the infant form of congenital glaucoma. The enlarged eye results from raised IOP before scleral maturation.

stem: You have been referred a case of open angle glaucoma. Which of the following would be an important point in diagnosing the case?
You have been referred a case of open angle glaucoma. Which of the following would be an important point in diagnosing the case?
explanation_verbatim: In open-angle glaucoma, optic disc cupping is a hallmark of progressive optic nerve damage due to increased IOP, even when the anterior chamber remains deep and open.

stem: On examining the fundus of one patient, multifocal yellowish grey patches with well demarcated borders were seen. Also there are other well defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy with pigmented borders. Which one of the following is the most probable diagnosis for such presentation?

On examining the fundus of one patient, multifocal yellowish grey patches with well demarcated borders were seen. Also there are other well defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy with pigmented borders. Which one of the following is the most probable diagnosis for such presentation?
explanation_verbatim: Multifocal yellow-gray lesions with pigmented borders on the fundus indicate choroiditis, an inflammatory condition of the choroid and retina. These can lead to scarring and atrophy.

stem: Visual acuity of a 2-year-old child can be tested by:
Visual acuity of a 2-year-old child can be tested by:
explanation_verbatim: For toddlers, visual acuity can be assessed using an optokinetic drum, which tests their ability to track moving stripes. It’s suitable for preverbal children.

stem: In pinhole test, the visual acuity gets better if the patient has:
In pinhole test, the visual acuity gets better if the patient has:
explanation_verbatim: Improvement of vision with a pinhole test indicates refractive error, as the pinhole eliminates peripheral light rays and improves focus on the retina.

stem: Photophobia can be due to:
Photophobia can be due to:
explanation_verbatim: Photophobia occurs when the cornea is inflamed or ulcerated due to irritation of corneal nerves. It’s not seen in retinal or lens conditions.

stem: Measuring corneal curvature is done using:
Measuring corneal curvature is done using:
explanation_verbatim: Corneal topography maps the curvature and shape of the cornea, useful for diagnosing keratoconus or planning refractive surgery.

stem: The normal range for intraocular pressure (IOP) as measured by applanation tonometry is:
The normal range for intraocular pressure (IOP) as measured by applanation tonometry is:
explanation_verbatim: The normal IOP range is 10–21 mmHg; values outside this may indicate ocular hypertension or glaucoma.

stem: In the management of diabetic retinopathy, optimal glycemic control is targeted to achieve which of the following HbA 1 c levels?
In the management of diabetic retinopathy, optimal glycemic control is targeted to achieve which of the following HbA 1 c levels?
explanation_verbatim: Optimal glycemic control in diabetic retinopathy aims for HbA1c around 7%, reducing the risk of progression and other microvascular complications.

stem: A 22-year-old male complains of double vision. Examination revealed esotropia, inability to abduct the left eye and face turn to the left side. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 22-year-old male complains of double vision. Examination revealed esotropia, inability to abduct the left eye and face turn to the left side. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Inability to abduct the left eye with esotropia indicates left lateral rectus weakness due to left abducent (VI) nerve palsy.

explanation_verbatim: When the lens is opaque, B-scan ultrasonography helps visualize the retina and posterior segment structures.

Examination revealed bilateral grayish brown ring around the limbus and separated from the limbus by a clear scleral zone. Which of the following would be the most important next step to do for such a patient?
explanation_verbatim: A corneal arcus (gray-brown ring) is common in the elderly; however, a lipid profile is recommended to rule out hyperlipidemia.

A 33-year-old woman presents with ptosis with S-shaped deformity of the upper eyelid. Examination revealed tenderness, edema and erythema of the outer third of the upper eyelid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_verbatim: Tender swelling at the outer upper eyelid with S-shaped ptosis indicates inflammation of the lacrimal gland (dacryoadenitis).

stem: Which of the following is the most common cause of vision impairment?
Which of the following is the most common cause of vision impairment?
explanation_verbatim: Globally, the most common cause of visual impairment is uncorrected refractive error (myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism).

stem: Orbital floor fractures are best assessed with which of the following diagnostic imaging modalities?
Orbital floor fractures are best assessed with which of the following diagnostic imaging modalities?
explanation_verbatim: Orbital floor fractures are best evaluated using CT coronal images, which clearly show the orbital floor and herniated tissues.

options: Conservative management as it is a self-limited condition

stem: A 80-year-old man presents to the GP with a complaint of severe eye pain, redness and decreased vision. Examination was carried out and it revealed that the redness had violet-bluish hue with scleral edema. Phenylephrine 10% was used topically for a few minutes but the redness didn't disappear. Which of the following would be the most appropriate next step in order to properly treat that patient?
options: Conservative management as it is a self-limited condition
explanation_verbatim: Severe eye pain with bluish scleral hue unresponsive to phenylephrine suggests scleritis, which may be linked to systemic disease and needs urgent specialist care.

stem: Which of the following is the best line of treatment used to control the acute inflammatory stage of thyroid eye disease?
Which of the following is the best line of treatment used to control the acute inflammatory stage of thyroid eye disease?
explanation_verbatim: The acute inflammatory phase of thyroid eye disease responds best to systemic corticosteroids to reduce orbital inflammation.

stem: Which of the following imaging modalities is absolutely contraindicated in a patient with intra-ocular metallic foreign body?
Which of the following imaging modalities is absolutely contraindicated in a patient with intra-ocular metallic foreign body?
explanation_verbatim: MRI is absolutely contraindicated in cases of metallic intraocular foreign bodies due to magnetic movement and heating risks.

stem: A 32-year-old woman sees an ophthalmologist as she suffers from eyelid drooping together with eye deviation outwards and downwards. Examination revealed unilateral mydriasis. Which of the following nerve paralysis is the cause of the patient's manifestations?

A 32-year-old woman sees an ophthalmologist as she suffers from eyelid drooping together with eye deviation outwards and downwards. Examination revealed unilateral mydriasis. Which of the following nerve paralysis is the cause of the patient's manifestations?
explanation_verbatim: Ptosis, “down and out” deviation, and a dilated pupil indicate oculomotor (III) nerve palsy, affecting most extraocular muscles and the sphincter pupillae.

stem: Which of the following increases the risk of central retinal vein occlusion?
Which of the following increases the risk of central retinal vein occlusion?
explanation_verbatim: Central retinal vein occlusion risk increases with oral contraceptive use due to hypercoagulability and venous stasis.

stem: Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?
Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?
explanation_verbatim: Arcuate scotoma is a characteristic visual field defect in glaucoma, corresponding to damage of arcuate nerve fibers near the optic disc.

stem: Following ocular trauma, a patient presented with enophthalmos and anesthesia of lower eyelid, cheek, side of nose, upper lip, upper teeth and gums. Which of the following is the nerve that is most probably involved in the trauma and caused these manifestations?

Following ocular trauma, a patient presented with enophthalmos and anesthesia of lower eyelid, cheek, side of nose, upper lip, upper teeth and gums. Which of the following is the nerve that is most probably involved in the trauma and caused these manifestations?
explanation_verbatim: Orbital floor fractures commonly injure the infraorbital nerve, causing numbness of the lower eyelid, cheek, and upper lip.
